summary.headline: Solarworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose 77% YoY to INR244 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5.9% and management cut FY27 margin guidance to 6–7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR244 crore, up about 77% YoY from INR137.9 crore, while EBITDA fell to INR15.2 crore from INR18.1 crore and PAT fell to INR4.2 crore from INR9.3 crore. H1 FY27 revenue doubled to INR412 crore with EBITDA of INR35.8 crore (8.3% margin) and PAT of INR13.7 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to metal and raw material price spikes locked into fixed-price PSU contracts won earlier, and guided FY28 as a much stronger year led by BESS, solar cell and module lines. The call was dominated by guidance credibility, margin pressure and shareholder-value questions, and management committed to return with short-term shareholder actions this quarter.

segments.name: Solar EPC and O&M
segments.commentary: Accounted for INR2,718 crore of the INR3,856 crore consolidated order book as of 31 Oct 2026. Management expects pure solar EPC to be about 30–40% of business in FY28.

segments.name: BESS EPC and BESS manufacturing
segments.commentary: BESS EPC order book of about INR1,138 crore (~30% of order book), with orders of 582 MW AC / 1.3 GWh DC from RRVUNL, GUVNL and NTPC. Management expects BESS to be about 50% of FY28 revenue, targeting INR1,500–1,800 crore.

segments.name: Solar manufacturing (modules, junction boxes, cells)
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW ALMM-listed module plant at Roorkee is operational and a 5 GW junction box line has started. The 2.4 GW TOPCon cell JV at Narmadapuram targets commercial production in June 2027, with an initial equity tranche of about INR26.8 crore paid on 30 Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,600–1,700 crore, with EBITDA margin of 6–7% and PAT margin of 5–6% (about INR80–90 crore PAT).
FY28 targets revenue of about INR3,000 crore and PAT of about INR200–220 crore, which management called a bumper year.
Management expects FY27 margins to stay under strain, with H2 margins improving as metal prices ease.
Target of INR5,000 crore revenue over the next 2–3 years.
Order book of INR3,856 crore; about INR1,100–1,200 crore to be executed in FY27 and about INR2,600 crore carried into FY28.
Board to revert to shareholders, likely in the current quarter, on short-term shareholder-value actions; no specific action was announced.
Solar cell line expected to start operating from Q2 FY28; BESS 2 GWh cell manufacturing facility decision expected by end-Nov or by 15 Dec 2026.
capex_capacity: 2.4 GW TOPCon solar cell JV at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh, targeted for commercial production in June 2027; 70–80% of output to be consumed internally, 15–20% sold externally.
Fully automated BESS manufacturing facility commissioned with KUKA robotics; about 1 GW of its capacity is covered by orders in hand.
1.5 GW module plant at Roorkee operational; 5 GW junction box line commenced.
Evaluating a 2 GWh lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in India; PLI application withdrawn due to crowding (about 23 bidders).
Utility BESS container cost about INR3.2 crore; in-house orders of about 300 containers, with 200–300 more under discussion from private developers, and a target of about 600 containers next year.
demand_pricing: Management said metal and lithium prices spiked and then fell: lithium carbonate fell from about 200,000 yuan/t six months ago to about 90,000 yuan/t, and copper and aluminium have started to fall.
Most revenue comes from PSU tenders (NTPC, SJVN, SECI) that are fixed price with no pass-through; private contracts do have pass-through, and some were renegotiated.
Raw material cost to revenue ratio fell from about 75% to about 59–60% in the period, which management attributed to revenue being front-loaded into H2 and to margin mismatch.
Solar cells quoted at about INR12–12.5 versus manufacturing cost of about INR6–6.5; management expects 15–20% margins in cell manufacturing, falling as capacity grows.
Management said about 200 GW of module capacity in India versus about 50 GW of expected installations, which is compressing module margins.
Two BESS IPP projects (GUVNL and RVUNL) target a minimum IRR of about 16%; the NTPC BESS project targets about 10% PAT margin.
Bids submitted worth about INR20,000 crore, largely PSU and including a large NTPC REL BESS order; two L1 orders worth INR1,271 crore are awaiting LOAs, expected in Nov or early Dec 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the profitability roadmap over 12 months, 2 years and 3 years, and what revised PAT guidance applies?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue INR1,600–1,700 crore at 6–7% EBITDA and 5–6% PAT margin (about INR80–90 crore PAT); FY28 revenue about INR3,000 crore and PAT about INR200–220 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What capital allocation or buyback steps will address the share price decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Board is evaluating short-term actions and will come back to shareholders probably in the current quarter; no specific buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Why did raw material costs fall as a share of sales, and is there hedging or pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs will converge to last year's percentage as H2 revenue dominates; forex on imported LC raw materials is hedged, but copper, steel and aluminium are not hedged, and PSU contracts are fixed price.

qa_highlights.question: Why was guidance cut from earlier PAT and margin expectations and why was the annual report pass-through language inconsistent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NTPC LOAs came 4–5 months after L1 (Oct 2025 bid, Feb–Mar 2026 LOA), so pre-procurement was not possible; delay was to avoid LDs, and turnover was held back to wait out prices; H2 margin improvement is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the BESS opportunity and how will it be captured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a utility-scale market of about 350–400 GWh over 5–6 years, plus C&I and residential segments; residential 1/2/5 kWh packs launched, and a C&I project of 125/261 kWh installed.

qa_highlights.question: How does one reconcile H1 PAT of INR13.7 crore with the FY27 PAT guidance of INR80–90 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 FY26 PAT was about INR100 crore against about INR20 crore in H1 FY26, and it is fairly confident of delivering the H2 FY27 balance.

risks_watch: Execution of fixed-price PSU contracts amid metal and raw material volatility; margins may stay below 10%.
Guidance credibility: FY27 revenue and margin guidance have been revised more than once, and FY27 PAT guidance is not yet met at H1.
Dependence on China-origin equipment for the 2.4 GW cell JV amid export pre-approval requirements; June 2027 timeline at risk.
Pending LOAs of INR1,271 crore from NTPC REL; timing dependent on NTPC board approval.
Shareholder-value action promised for this quarter; watch for buyback or other concrete steps.
Sustainability of BESS IRRs and the planned sale of BESS IPP projects, and the decision on the 2 GWh cell facility (end-Nov or 15 Dec 2026).
Management expects solar EPC slowdown for about 12 more months due to grid connectivity issues.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and FY28 and BESS, but defensive and candid on FY27 margin shortfall, which management attributed to raw material spikes and PSU fixed-price contracts. Answers on shareholder returns and the margin guidance cut were non-committal, deferring concrete action to the board's next update.
key_quotes: We believe that our margins will significantly improve.
So, we believe while FY27 margins will remain under strain, FY28 should be a bumper year for Solarworld.
Our motto is that we should be India's leading backward integrated EPC company and not a leading manufacturer.
So, we will come back to the shareholders probably in the current quarter on what short-term actions we will take to create shareholder value.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,600-1,700 crore (roughly 2x FY26 implied by H1 doubling), backed by a INR3,856 crore order book with about INR1,100-1,200 crore to execute in FY27, plus FY28 target of about INR3,000 crore backed by Roorkee modules, BESS orders (582 MW AC) and a 2.4 GW cell JV only due June 2027; FY27 margin guidance was cut to 6-7% EBITDA / 5-6% PAT and management flagged a 12-month so

quality.why: Revenue rose 77% YoY to INR244 crore in Q2 FY27, but the brief does not state whether volume, price or mix drove it, and names no one-off gain, loss or low base; management's own explanation centres on margins and front-loaded H2 revenue, not on what drove the top-line growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 5.9% in Q2 and 8.3% in H1 against FY27 guide of 6-7%, but management expects H2 margins to improve as metal prices ease (lithium carbonate down from ~200,000 to ~90,000 yuan/t) and raw material ratio converges to last year's level; PSU fixed-price contracts limit upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 2.4 GW TOPCon cell JV at Narmadapuram targeted for commercial production June 2027 with INR26.8 crore initial equity paid, and solar cell line expected to start from Q2 FY28; Roorkee 1.5 GW modules already operational, so new capacity lands inside the window but depends on China-origin equipment and export approvals.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided to INR1,600-1,700 crore for FY27 (about 2x FY26 implied by H1 at INR412 crore) and INR3,000 crore for FY28, backed by INR3,856 crore order book with INR1,100-1,200 crore to execute in FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Decision on a 2 GWh BESS lithium-ion cell facility is due by end-Nov or 15 Dec 2026 after PLI application was withdrawn, and BESS demand (582 MW AC / 1.3 GWh DC orders, ~600 containers targeted next year) is pulling capacity needs.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue and margin guidance were already cut and revised more than once, and FY27 PAT of INR80-90 crore is not met at H1 (PAT INR13.7 crore), so upgrades look unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 PAT of INR80-90 crore needs about INR66-76 crore in H2 against INR13.7 crore in H1, module margins are compressed by ~200 GW capacity vs ~50 GW installs, and LOAs of INR1,271 crore are pending NTPC REL approval.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Residential 1/2/5 kWh BESS packs already launched and C&I project of 125/261 kWh installed, with utility BESS containers ramping to ~600 next year; new product lines (cells) start from Q2 FY28.

rows.label: Pending NTPC REL BESS LOAs worth INR1,271 crore
rows.why: Two L1 orders worth INR1,271 crore are awaiting LOAs expected in Nov or early Dec 2026, against an order book of INR3,856 crore, though timing depends on NTPC board approval.

rows.label: Short-term shareholder-value action
rows.why: Board committed to revert to shareholders probably in the current quarter on short-term shareholder-value actions after share price decline, but no specific buyback or action was announced.

rows.label: Solar cell margin normalisation
rows.why: Cells quoted at INR12-12.5 vs cost INR6-6.5 implies 15-20% margins today, which management expects to fall as capacity grows, so cell margin upside is conditional on pricing holding.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY28 (about INR3,000 crore revenue, INR200-220 crore PAT), BESS and cell JV, but cautious and defensive on the FY27 margin cut, attributing it to metal spikes and PSU fixed-price contracts; analysts pressed on guidance credibility, the H1-to-H2 PAT gap and shareholder-val
